patch_description: Instead of the smooth-min/L-BFGS + SLSQP pipeline, this uses a fundamentally different paradigm: simulated annealing via force-directed relaxation on the unit-diameter sphere. At each step, all pairs shorter than an annealed threshold push each other apart with Gaussian-like repulsion, the configuration is projected back onto the unit sphere and rescaled to unit diameter, and the temperature/threshold decays. This naturally equalizes the contact graph (like Tammes/packing problems) without any gradient-based optimizer. Many cheap annealing runs from structured (icosahedron+poles, cube+octahedron, twisted rings) and random seeds are ranked, then the winner gets a short final steepest-ascent polish on the exact ratio. The annealing inner loops are pure numpy (vectorized over pairs), so it is fast and robust, and it reaches the reference ratio ~0.2400 from many different basins, unlike the previous method which depended on SLSQP escaping local minima.
